2608.07068.title: MemOPD: On-Policy Distillation through Memory State Alignment for Long-Horizon Agents
2608.07068.paper_summary: Long-horizon agents accumulate growing contexts during interaction, impairing performance and stability. Compact memory mitigates this problem by compressing and rewriting the history retained between model invocations. Learning what to retain typically relies on proximal policy optimization (PPO) with final task rewards, but sparse rewards provide little guidance for individual memory updates. This limitation motivates on-policy distillation (OPD), which supplies dense teacher supervision on student rollouts. For such supervision to be valid, the teacher must evaluate each sampled action under the same state in which it was generated. However, the context rewriting performed during memory compression can break this alignment. When sampled responses are retained and re-encoded for later invocations, flattening the interaction into a persistent history may cause the teacher to score the action under a state that the student never visited during rollout. The action therefore remains on-policy by provenance, but not necessarily by state. We therefore propose Memory-Aligned On-Policy Distillation (MemOPD). MemOPD records the inputs and sampled outputs of each model invocation, restores its original token positions and causal visibility, and packs the reconstructed invocations for efficient teacher scoring. The teacher provides full-vocabulary supervision at the sampled action positions, while PPO preserves the final task objective. Experiments verify state alignment across several context updates and show that it improves F1 by 7.0% over persistent-history teacher scoring in a matched control. Overall, MemOPD-3B improves F1 over PPO by up to 416.2%, while packing yields up to a 1.63x speedup in actor computation during training. The code for this work is publicly available at: https://github.com/TPssp/MemOPD.
2608.07068.paper_summary_zh: 長期代理在互動過程中累積不斷增長的上下文，這會影響性能和穩定性。緊湊的記憶通過壓縮和重寫模型調用之間保留的歷史來緩解這一問題。學習保留什麼通常依賴於最接近的策略優化（PPO）和最終任務獎勵，但稀疏獎勵對個別記憶更新提供的指導有限。這一限制促使了在線策略蒸餾（OPD）的提出，它在學生的回合中提供了密集的教師監督。為了使這種監督有效，教師必須在生成每個樣本動作的相同狀態下評估它。然而，在記憶壓縮過程中執行的上下文重寫可能會打破這種對齊。當保留的樣本回應被重新編碼以供後續調用時，將互動展平為持久的歷史可能會導致教師在學生在回合中從未訪問過的狀態下評分該動作。因此，該動作在來源上仍然是在線的，但不一定在狀態上。因此，我們提出了記憶對齊在線策略蒸餾（MemOPD）。MemOPD記錄每次模型調用的輸入和樣本輸出，恢復其原始標記位置和因果可見性，並打包重建的調用以便於教師評分。教師在樣本動作位置提供全詞彙監督，而PPO則保持最終任務目標。實驗驗證了幾個上下文更新中的狀態對齊，並顯示它在匹配控制中將F1提高了7.0%。總體而言，MemOPD-3B在F1上比PPO提高了最多416.2%，而打包在訓練期間的演員計算中可實現最多1.63倍的加速。這項工作的代碼可在以下網址公開獲得：https://github.com/TPssp/MemOPD。
